#5407. Nissan expects to sell some hybrid-only models in the U.S. around 2030, on its own timeline

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Nissan's Americas chairman says there is no need to rush, as Toyota sells hybrid-only models and Honda plans a hybrid-only CR-V

Nissan anticipates introducing hybrid-only versions of certain models in the U.S. around 2030, a more gradual pace than Toyota $TM and Honda $HMC have set, according to Bloomberg.

"We're getting ready to be full hybrid, maybe in 2030, but I don't think it's necessary to do it too quickly," Christian Meunier, chairman of Nissan Americas, told reporters in Detroit on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg. "We need to put the technology on at the right time, and at the right cost," he said.

The timeline covers only those nameplates where Nissan would drop the gas-only option entirely, according to The Associated Press. The AP said the company’s near-term priority is to get its hybrid system established with buyers, and only afterward settle on a pace for retiring conventional versions.

Meunier said buyers on tight budgets can still turn to gas-only vehicles, since certain hybrids cost $2,000 to $2,500 more, according to Bloomberg. He said the premium can shrink as production volume rises, as it has for Toyota.

Nissan is overhauling its plants and expanding its network of suppliers to support hybrid output, according to Bloomberg. It plans to start production of the completely new Xterra, a midsize SUV that will offer a hybrid variant, at its Canton, Mississippi, plant in 2028, Bloomberg said.

Toyota already sells a number of models only as hybrids, among them the RAV4, Camry and Sienna, according to Bloomberg. Honda said last week it will sell the 2028 CR-V with a hybrid powertrain only when the seventh-generation model arrives next year.

Nissan unveiled the 2027 Rogue with its e-Power hybrid system in September. In that system, the gasoline engine generates electricity for the drive motors, and the car needs no external charger. The Rogue is Nissan's top seller in the U.S. and competes with the Toyota RAV4 and Honda CR-V, which Meunier named as the Rogue's direct target.

Nissan announced on Oct. 30 that a limited number of Rogue Hybrid SR models would reach dealerships in late November, with SV, SR and Platinum versions due in early 2027, according to the AP. The AP said Nissan plans to show the Rogue Hybrid at the Los Angeles Auto Show, which runs from Nov. 20 to Nov. 29.

#5406. Road to Esports Nations Cup 2027 Gives National Teams More Chances to Compete and Fans More Matches to Follow

All countries and territories that qualified in 2026 retain their places, following a first qualification season involving nearly 200,000 players.

RIYADH, Saudi Arabia, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Esports Foundation (EF) today announced the Esports Nations Cup's expanded Road to ENC 2027, with events run by National Team Partners (NTPs), new qualification tournaments, larger national rosters, and the ENC Ranking.

The Road to ENC 2027 gives players more chances to represent their countries and territories. National teams will have more opportunities to compete, creating new rivalries for fans throughout the season, while building momentum toward the inaugural Esports Nations Cup Finals in November 2027.

Nearly 200,000 players competed in 210 regional qualifiers during the first ENC qualification season, with 2,000 players from 123 countries and territories helping secure places at the Esports Nations Cup. Every place earned by a national team in 2026 will be protected, with players who represented those countries and territories included in ENC's expanded national rosters, from which coaches will select their Finals squads.

Countries and territories yet to qualify will also have another route through new regional online tournaments leading into a final LAN qualifier. Regional online qualifiers will kick off February 26, 2027, and run over five weeks across multiple game titles. The game-specific dates and final LAN qualifier details will be announced at a later date.

"Representing your nation is one of the proudest moments in any athlete's career. For fans, supporting their country or territory can be their first connection to a sport and the beginning of a lasting passion," said Ralf Reichert, CEO of the Esports Foundation. "As we build towards the first Esports Nations Cup, we want to help national teams grow together and give fans a team to believe in. Road to ENC creates more opportunities for those teams to compete and for fans to get to know the players, follow emerging rivalries, and become a part of their team's journey. When those teams arrive at ENC 2027, we want fans to have been part of how they got there."

Four elements will support national teams on the Road to the Finals:

National Team Partner-led events will give fans more opportunities to watch and support their national team before the Finals. National Team Partners can organize local activations, friendly matches, and multi-nation invitationals, creating more competitions while giving coaches opportunities to test new players. Supported through the ENC Development Fund, these events are designed to build national fandom and a stronger local esports ecosystem. National Team Partners can submit proposals for 2027 events until the end of December 2026.

New qualification tournaments will give countries and territories that missed out in 2026 another route to ENC. Teams will face off in regional online qualifiers, with seven regional winners and one invited nation from the ENC Solidarity program advancing to a final LAN qualifier to compete for the remaining places.

Expanded national rosters give coaches more flexibility to develop their teams. National team coaches can add eligible players to the squads that qualified in 2026, allowing them to test different combinations in national team matches before selecting their Finals lineups by May 31, 2027. Updated expanded rosters are due by January 15, 2027. For solo titles, the earned slot remains with the player who qualified for their country or territory.

The ENC Ranking will create year-round competitive stakes and give fans a live view of where their country or territory stands throughout the season. Players will earn points for their national teams through results in international Club leagues and tournaments, as well as national team competitions. The standings will evolve as players compete throughout the season, helping determine seeding for the ENC's group stage draw and informing direct invitations to future editions of ENC.

More details about the ENC Ranking, the schedule for the new qualifiers, and NTP-led events will be announced in the coming weeks.

To learn more about the Esports Nations Cup, visit the ENC website or follow the Esports Foundation on LinkedIn.

About the Esports Nations CupThe Esports Nations Cup (ENC) is a global international esports competition for nations and territories. Bringing together leading players to represent their countries across multiple game titles, ENC is designed to create a new platform for national pride, elite competition and long-term ecosystem development.

#5405. Crypto futures are implying Anthropic is worth more than its IPO price range

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Contracts tied to Anthropic's Nasdaq debut on Thursday imply about $1.7 trillion, against $1.4 trillion at the top of the range

Anthropic is being priced at roughly $1.7 trillion in crypto futures markets, exceeding the $1.4 trillion value tied to the high end of its planned IPO range, according to Bloomberg.

Anthropic is expected to set its IPO price higher than the $70 to $78 a share it is currently marketing, according to CNBC, citing unnamed sources. CNBC also said the company plans to list on the Nasdaq $NDAQ under the ticker ANT.

The contracts are called perpetual futures since they have no expiration date. They give traders a way to speculate on Anthropic's share price after listing without owning any shares, according to Bloomberg. Holding them gives a trader no stake in the company and no vote in its affairs.

Trade.xyz, a derivatives issuer built on the Hyperliquid blockchain, has seen its contracts drop by as much as 21% since Nov. 4, reaching about $97 in Asia trading on Wednesday. That puts the price about 24% higher than the $78 ceiling of the proposed range, according to Bloomberg.

The AI trade has been under strain since voters went to the polls in the U.S. midterms, as fears of a bubble and outsized spending pressure shares, according to Bloomberg. Nvidia $NVDA stock has also been hit by the exit of CEO Jensen Huang.

"The perps market is still positioned for a pop, just a smaller one than it was pricing a week ago," said Kelly Ye, head of research at Talos, according to Bloomberg.

The futures have not always matched debut prices. SpaceX stock began trading in June at $150, which topped its $135 offer price yet fell short of the $176 its futures had reached earlier the same morning, according to Bloomberg. Futures for Cerebras Systems were priced no more than 3% away from its opening-day price one hour ahead of the first trades. "Pre-IPO perps aren't a crystal ball," Ye said.

Anthropic perpetuals on Binance and Hyperliquid had about $422 million in open interest two days ahead of the anticipated debut, versus $251 million for SpaceX contracts at a similar point, according to Bloomberg. It said 20 wallets hold more than two-thirds of the positions in the Trade.xyz contract, and each $1 million in net purchases or sales shifts that market by about 2%.

Nvidia announced last week that Huang had resigned as president, CEO and board member days before the offering. Nvidia has committed about $10 billion to buy Anthropic stock in a $26 billion private placement set to close alongside the IPO.

Anthropic’s offering could bring in as much as $64.4 billion at the top of the range, split between the company and its shareholders, according to Bloomberg. Goldman Sachs $GS and Morgan Stanley $MS are leading the offering, and Altimeter Capital plans to commit $5 billion to it.

#5403. OneTrust’s Fall ’26 Release expands AI visibility, privacy and third-party risk tools

Governance platform provider OneTrust LLC today announced its Fall ’26 Release, a set of platform updates said to bring governance into the workflows where business decisions are made.

Leading the list of updates is a revised AI inventory, which is designed to reflect changes across a customer’s environment on a continuous basis. According to OneTrust, the change is needed because many organizations running complex networks of AI systems and agents have only limited visibility into how those systems operate. Model associations, potential matches and deprecation indicators from providers are now pulled into the inventory from a curated library of foundation models.

Relationships among AI systems, models, agents, projects, risks, controls and workflows can be explored through an interactive AI lineage view. AI performance and operational dashboards, added in the release, bring usage, associated risk, evaluation coverage, outbound personally identifiable information discovery and token consumption into one summary.

On the third-party risk side, a workflow rule that launches a risk assessment can now trigger OneTrust’s Deep Research AI skill. The in-depth research report that the skill compiles from public data sources is then used to answer the assessment questionnaire. OneTrust claims the integration can cut the time needed to complete a third-party risk assessment from weeks to minutes.

Drawing on previous assessments and supplier documentation, the company’s expanded AI Document Scanning and Inventory Response Analysis features can now also answer questions about the business engagement tied to a third party.

In the company’s consent management platform, navigation, configuration, scanning, publishing and geolocation management have also been brought into a single workflow under a modernized interface.

OneTrust is sharing availability details for the Fall ’26 Release through an overview webinar.

OneTrust has raised $1.13 billion to date, including $150 million in 2023 at a valuation of $4.5 billion. Investors in the company include Insight Partners LP, Coatue Management, Technology Crossover Ventures LP, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 LP, Franklin Resources Inc., Generation Investment Management LLP and Sands Capital Management.

#5402. House Democrats are probing whether Lutnick shielded Cantor Fitzgerald's Nvidia stake

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Three ranking members are demanding records from the firm his son chairs, and Cantor Fitzgerald says the allegations are baseless

Bonnie Cash/UPI/Bloomberg via Getty Images

House Democrats are investigating whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick used his office to protect the Nvidia $NVDA holdings of Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm chaired by his son, and are demanding records from the firm.

Rep. Jamie Raskin, a Maryland Democrat and ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee, Rep. Gregory Meeks, a New York Democrat and ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove, a California Democrat and ranking member of the Foreign Affairs subcommittee on South and Central Asia, sent a letter to Cantor Fitzgerald Chairman Brandon Lutnick and announced it Wednesday. They want to know whether Howard Lutnick blocked efforts to stop suspected smuggling of advanced Nvidia chips to China while the firm held hundreds of millions of dollars in Nvidia stock.

"[T]he American people deserve to know: Did the Secretary of Commerce seriously and perhaps irreversibly compromise U.S. national security interests to make money for his adult children and Cantor Fitzgerald?" the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers are seeking records of every Nvidia trade the firm has made since January 2024 and an accounting of its business in China and Southeast Asia. They also want communications about export controls and suspected chip smuggling, communications with the Commerce Department about Nvidia, Megaspeed and Asian data center projects, and records on President Donald Trump's reported Nvidia investments.

The letter asks Cantor Fitzgerald to preserve all relevant records, including encrypted messages and business communications on personal devices. It sets a Dec. 1 deadline for written confirmation.

Before Howard Lutnick became commerce secretary, Cantor Fitzgerald had disclosed holding more than 3.5 million shares of Nvidia stock, according to the lawmakers. After his confirmation, he agreed to transfer ownership of the firm to trusts benefiting his adult children. While U.S. officials scrutinized Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer, Cantor Fitzgerald cut its reported Nvidia holdings by close to half. It held about $310 million in Nvidia stock at the end of March.

The letter follows the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted to extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected of spying for China. The lawmakers say Howard Lutnick resisted pressure to cut off Megaspeed’s access to Nvidia chips. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said four federal agencies had backed blacklisting Megaspeed for months while Commerce, which controls the blacklist, held out.

Cantor Fitzgerald told CNBC the letter contained errors and that any suggestion the firm's business swayed decisions made by the government has no basis. The firm said it has no meaningful position of its own in Nvidia, and that the shares it carries mostly stem from equity swaps it entered into on behalf of clients, with the drop coming as hedges were wound down once clients exited their positions. A Cantor Fitzgerald spokesperson said the firm plays no part in deciding U.S. export controls or which companies land on the entity list, according to Bloomberg. The Commerce Department and Nvidia did not respond right away when asked to comment.

Bessent said on Nov. 13 that the Commerce Department decides whether Megaspeed is added to the export blacklist, and that the Treasury, State and Defense departments and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all supported listing it.

Howard Lutnick has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Committee Chair Tim Scott, a South Carolina Republican, has requested his testimony on Dec. 10.

#5401. Moso Networks, SOLiD and CTS Introduce Managed CBRS for DAS, Bringing Private Wireless to Existing In-Building Infrastructure

SACRAMENTO, Calif., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Moso Networks, a leader in private 5G infrastructure and management solutions, today announced a strategic collaboration with SOLiD, a leading provider of Distributed Antenna System (DAS) infrastructure, and Communication Technology Services (CTS), a leading national in-building wireless systems integrator, to help enterprises transform traditional in-building cellular systems into converged wireless platforms capable of supporting both carrier services and private wireless networks.

Historically, deploying private wireless alongside DAS could require additional in-building distribution infrastructure, adding cost and complexity for enterprises seeking both carrier coverage and dedicated private cellular connectivity. While each service retains its own network components, the collaboration between Moso Networks, SOLiD, and CTS makes it more practical and economical to share the DAS distribution infrastructureâreducing duplication, lowering deployment costs, and helping enterprises get more value from their wireless investments.

By leveraging the shared-spectrum framework established under FCC Part 96, organizations can deploy a converged, in-building wireless architecture that supports both licensed carrier services and secure enterprise private networks. This approach enables building owners to maximize existing DAS investments while introducing dedicated wireless connectivity for operational technology, IoT, automation, security, and other business-critical applications without deploying an entirely separate network infrastructure.

"Building owners and enterprises need to provide reliable indoor carrier coverage, and now they can get more from that investment," said Stephen Leotis, CEO of Moso Networks. "Extending DAS with CBRS private wireless lowers a major barrier to private 5G adoption, which is the cost of building a completely separate in-building network. Enterprises can now serve people and operations from the same distribution infrastructure."

The solution combines SOLiD's carrier-grade DAS infrastructure with Moso Networks' CBRS-based private wireless platform to create a converged in-building wireless architecture that supports both public cellular services and enterprise private network applications over shared DAS distribution infrastructure, while maintaining the distinct network components required for each service. SOLiD's ALLIANCE DAS platform distributes licensed carrier signals throughout a facility while simultaneously transporting CBRS spectrum across the same antenna infrastructure. Moso's private wireless solution provides the CBRS radio access network (RAN), spectrum management, and core network capabilities required to deliver secure, dedicated wireless connectivity for enterprise devices and operational applications.

Together, the integrated architecture enables organizations to leverage shared DAS distribution infrastructure for carrier coverage, voice services, mobile broadband, and CBRS-based private wireless applications such as IoT devices, automation systems, security platforms, and mission-critical communications. The result is a scalable, future-ready wireless platform that simplifies deployment, reduces infrastructure costs, and enables enterprises to support both occupant connectivity and operational technology requirements from a common in-building wireless infrastructure.

CTS brings the engineering expertise and systems integration capabilities needed to turn this converged architecture into a practical, deployable solution. As a national in-building wireless integrator, CTS designs, deploys, integrates, and commissions DAS and private cellular networks, bringing together SOLiD's DAS infrastructure and Moso Networks' CBRS technology to support both commercial carrier services and enterprise private wireless applications through a shared distribution infrastructure.

Beyond initial deployment, CTS provides ongoing monitoring, maintenance, performance optimization, and lifecycle support, allowing enterprises to rely on a single partner for implementation and long-term network operations.

"For enterprises already investing in DAS, deploying a separate private cellular network can mean duplicating portions of the in-building infrastructure," said Dr. Juanyu Bu, Executive Vice President of Engineering at CTS. "By integrating CBRS into a shared DAS distribution architecture, we have an opportunity to reduce that duplication and improve the economics of private cellular deployment. The key is engineering a solution that meets the performance requirements of both carrier services and enterprise private wireless networks."

The solution is particularly attractive for commercial real estate owners, healthcare systems, manufacturing facilities, higher education campuses, airports, transportation hubs, logistics centers, and large public venues where both carrier coverage and operational connectivity are essential.

"As enterprises continue to expand their wireless requirements, infrastructure flexibility becomes increasingly important," said Shane Hague, Senior VP, Sales and Business Development at SOLiD. For years, DAS has been the answer for indoor cellular coverage. Now it can be much more. Together, Moso Networks, SOLiD, and CTS are helping organizations evolve existing in-building wireless infrastructure into a platform that delivers carrier coverage, private wireless, and the flexibility to support the next generation of enterprise wireless applications.

#5400. FDA is stepping up unannounced inspections at Indian pharmaceutical facilities

Free daily briefing on global business news.

The agency conducted 87% of its India audits without prior notice in the year ended March 31, up from 47% a year earlier

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is conducting unannounced inspections at Indian drug facilities, an agency official said at an event in Mumbai, according to Bloomberg.

"Previously, an inspection had to be coordinated through our local counterparts or public health authorities. Now those are unannounced," said Neil Bonzagni, an international relations specialist at the FDA.

The agency conducted 87% of its audits in India without advance warning during the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30, versus 47% a year earlier, according to Bloomberg. Bloomberg cited Elizabeth Miller, associate commissioner at the FDA’s office of inspections and investigations, for the figures.

India has more FDA-approved facilities than any other country outside the U.S., and its manufacturers provide roughly 40% of the generic drugs consumed by Americans, according to Bloomberg.

Quality concerns have followed Indian drug exports, according to Bloomberg. Dozens of children in Gambia and Uzbekistan died following their use of Indian-made cough syrups, and four Americans were killed by eyedrops from the country that were contaminated with bacteria. Those deaths occurred in 2022 and 2023.

Bonzagni said the FDA assesses the supply chain "from cradle to grave," from the sourcing of ingredients through production and the distribution of final goods, according to Bloomberg. "The unannounced inspections really do help us ensure safety there," he said.

#5398. Tesorai raises $5.3M to feed starving AI models with biological data and accelerate drug discovery

Drug researchers and medical laboratories generate massive volumes of biological data every single day, yet somehow the artificial intelligence models designed to speed up drug discovery are still starved of useful information.

It’s a strange paradox, but a startup called Tesorai Inc. believes it has the solution after raising $5.3 million in seed funding today.

The round was led by Perplexity Fund, IQT and South Central Ventures, and saw New Stack Ventures, NextGen Venture Partners, f7 Ventures, VitalStage Ventures and ZAKA participating. With its completion, Tesorai has now raised $8 million in total, and will use that money to try to accelerate AI-driven scientific discovery by digging deeper into existing datasets to surface the deeply buried insights that human researchers have missed.

Biological data covers a broad spectrum spanning genetic sequences to protein measurements, and metabolomic processes to cellular imaging. This information is extremely valuable to drug researchers, because it serves as the primary fuel for training advanced AI models that can predict disease pathways and identify new therapies.

AI-accelerated drug discovery is seen as one of the most promising use cases for this technology, but it hasn’t yet managed to change the world in the same way that generative AI has done. Why not? Because researchers still don’t have nearly enough of it, which limits the accuracy of the best models they’ve come up with so far.

To combat this scarcity of biological data, tech giants including OpenAI Group PBC, Google LLC’s DeepMind, Meta Platforms Inc., Isomorphic Labs Inc. and others are spending billions of dollars to generate more of it, but Tesorai’s co-founders Charlie Kim, Melissa Miao and Peter Cimermancic believe it’s also possible to do more with less.

To that end, Tesorai’s goal is to unlock the biological data that researchers already have access to. Rather than using the summarized findings available in published research papers and clinical studies, it uses AI to analyze raw spectrometry data generated by lab instruments.

Its platform consists of Tesorai Search, which rapidly ingests and analyzes terabytes of data from different sources. There’s also Tesorai Chat, which is used by scientists to ask questions of biological datasets in plain English. And there’s Tesorai Trove, a curated catalog of thousands of publicly available datasets and studies.

Those three components work together to process the raw instrument data from both new and historical lab studies and experiments, before analyzing it thoroughly to try to surface insights that were missed by their authors. By using those insights, Tesorai believes it can train more accurate AI models for drug discovery and therapy research.

“Life science R&D is accelerating and becoming increasingly autonomous, which makes it more important to extract as much insight as possible from every experiment,” Chief Scientific Officer Kim explained. “Tesorai does this for a lab’s new data and for thousands of published studies, and the gains compound as each experiment builds on the last. Ultimately, this will help the industry to develop better medicines faster.”

The startup points to a number of discoveries it has unearthed that were missed by previous studies. In one example, Tesorai reprocessed and re-crunched the data from five studies of the human brain in Alzheimer’s disease-afflicted patients. Through its analysis, it identified a key Alzheimer’s biomarker called p-tau217 that was missed in all five of the studies.

Its findings were published in JAMA Neurology in August. In another example, Tesorai illustrated how it was able to accelerate AI model training by adding protein data to a small single-cell AI model, enabling it to beat larger RNA-only models, including one with 40 times more parameters, on multiple benchmarks.

Miao, who’s Tesorai’s chief executive officer, said basically every scientific study produces much more data than what’s reported by its authors. Moreover, most of those studies are never revisited. “Our platform reclaims the value of experiments that have already been done and amplifies each new experiment with the relevant evidence that already exists,” she said.

Tesorai’s early success has paved the way for its initial traction, and it has already established partnerships with the MD Anderson Cancer Center, New York University and the Michael J. Fox Foundation. With the funds from today’s round, it will try to secure more partnerships with the life sciences industry, catalog more public studies and expand its platform to cover other molecular data beyond proteins and genomes.

Perplexity Fund General Partner Joanna Lee Shevelenko said it’s clear that AI can dramatically accelerate scientific research, and that’s why it needs as much high-quality experimental data as possible. “Tesorai is building the infrastructure to make that data usable at scale, giving scientists and AI systems a stronger foundation for advancing research,” she said.

#5395. Exchange Ledgers in the Middle as CFTC and SEC Diverge on What “Delivery” Means

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

A customer buys a token on a U.S. exchange and the app shows the balance. Under the CFTC's December 14 framework, nothing has been delivered yet.

Under the SEC's crypto proposal, delivery doesn't decide the question at all. An October 27 comment letter asks the two agencies to settle on one answer.

Open almost any crypto exchange app after a purchase and you'll see a clean number: 1.0000 ETH, available. To the customer, the asset is theirs. To the exchange's database, it's a row in an internal ledger. To federal regulators, that row is now being judged by two different tests that don't agree on what it means.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has opened an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on what it calls Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions (CTX) and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets (CAM). It sets out the agency's first formal view of "actual delivery" for crypto since it withdrew its 2020 guidance last December. Comments close on December 14.

The Securities and Exchange Commission's Regulation Crypto Assets proposal takes a different view of the same moment. Then, on October 27, a comment letter on the SEC's file raised the gap directly. It described the situation as "two conflicting definitions of the same physical facts" and asked the agencies to "please coordinate the definitions."

Delivery matters because it decides which rulebook applies.

For the CFTC, the answer comes from Section 2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act. A leveraged, margined or financed retail commodity trade is treated like a futures contract unless "actual delivery" happens within 28 days. If delivery happens in time, the trade falls outside futures rules. If it doesn't, the exchange is effectively running a futures venue.

For the SEC, the question is whether a token is still part of an investment contract. Under the August proposal, a covered investment contract ends when the issuer has finished or permanently stopped its essential managerial efforts and files a Form TR transition report. Whether the buyer has received the token is not part of that test.

So one agency treats delivery as the deciding question, and the other barely considers it.

The CFTC's position is still preliminary, but it is detailed. Published in the Federal Register on October 13, the notice relies on the Monex case standard: actual delivery requires "the transfer of some meaningful degree of possession or control."

For crypto, the agency suggests that possession and control "may require possession of the credentials (e.g., private key(s))." It takes three positions that matter most to exchanges:

The agency is also asking whether control has to be exclusive, whether delivery can happen while a lien or security interest is outstanding, and how financing offered in an exchange's standard account documents affects whether a trade is covered at all.

The SEC's proposal, released on August 18, deals with a different question. It creates offering exemptions, including a $5 million startup exemption over four years, and a safe harbor for when a crypto asset's investment contract ends. Neither depends on where the token sits.

Under the proposal, a token held in a customer's self-custody wallet and a token recorded on an exchange's books are treated the same way. In both cases, the investment contract question depends on the issuer's managerial efforts and its filings.

That is the gap the October 27 letter tries to close. Its author, who describes themselves as a fintech founder designing a consumer platform, argues that "where the customer holds the private keys or execution is on-chain, with custody evidence, the asset should be treated as delivered and the covered-investment-contract analysis should end there."

Running four common exchange transactions through both frameworks shows where the tests split.

Trade one: a fully paid purchase left on the exchange.

Trade two: the same purchase withdrawn to a self-custody wallet on day three.

Trade three: a margined purchase kept on the exchange's ledger for 30 days.

Trade four: an on-chain swap that settles directly into the user's wallet.

The pattern is consistent. Self-custody is the only position that clearly counts as delivery under the CFTC's view and also ends the analysis under the letter's proposed SEC fix. Everything left on an exchange's internal ledger stays in an unclear position. The CFTC treats it as undelivered and the SEC's text doesn't address it.

The letter was filed on October 27, a week after the SEC's October 20 comment deadline. It is anonymous and brief, but its main concern is practical. If the definitions stay separate, it warns, founders will have to design products around whichever rule is stricter.

It is the only filing on either docket so far that sets the two definitions side by side.

The CFTC process is still at the advance-notice stage, so a formal proposal will follow. For U.S. platforms, though, the direction is clear. Under the CFTC's preliminary reading, an exchange that keeps customer assets in internal ledger accounts has not delivered them. If that exchange also offers margin or financing, it is on track to be treated as a futures venue.

The SEC's final rule could adopt the letter's custody-based approach or keep delivery out of its analysis entirely. Until one of those happens, the same ledger entry can be undelivered for one regulator and irrelevant for the other.

Exchanges and their customers have until December 14 to say which definition should prevail. The real decision is whether "delivered" ends up meaning the same thing at both agencies.

TJX Companies $TJX raised its full-year outlook on Wednesday, projecting comparable sales growth of 4% for the fiscal year after the owner of T.J. Maxx, Marshalls and HomeGoods reported third-quarter results above its plan.

CEO and President Ernie Herrman said unseasonably mild conditions across the U.S. and Canada have softened sales in certain categories, though the company expects momentum to build through the holiday season, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Third-quarter comparable sales rose 4%. Net sales rose 6% to $15.95 billion, and net income was $1.54 billion, or $1.39 per diluted share, up 9% from a year earlier. Adjusted earnings, which exclude a benefit from tariff refunds, were $1.34 per share, up 5%.

Comparable sales at Marmaxx, the division that includes T.J. Maxx, Marshalls and Sierra in the U.S., rose 2% on top of a 6% gain a year earlier. HomeGoods, TJX Canada and TJX International also posted gains. Herrman expects further improvement at Marmaxx in the fourth quarter, according to The Wall Street Journal.

For the fourth quarter, TJX plans consolidated comparable sales growth of 2% to 3%. It expects a pretax profit margin of 11.5% to 11.6%, or 11.8% to 11.9% excluding costs tied to tariff refunds, and adjusted earnings of $1.42 to $1.45 per share.

For the full year, TJX expects a pretax profit margin of 12.4%. It continues to expect an adjusted pretax margin of 12.0% to 12.1%. The company expects adjusted earnings of $5.17 to $5.20 per share, which raises the low end of a prior range of $5.15 to $5.20.

TJX received $132 million in refunds of tariffs it paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act during the third quarter and $463 million over the first nine months. The net benefit to third-quarter pretax profit was $77 million. The company does not expect additional refunds in the fourth quarter. Adjusted pretax profit margin for the third quarter was 12.5%, down 0.2 percentage point from a year earlier. TJX returned $1.5 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends during the quarter.

TJX stock rose 6.6% to $138.42 in premarket trading.

In August, TJX raised its full-year profit forecast after second-quarter results while keeping its comparable sales outlook at 3% to 4%. Marmaxx comparable sales rose 1% in the second quarter. The company guided to third-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.30 to $1.32 per share.

#5391. Reson8 releases Rumble-2-Flash speech model as a free open-weights download

Amsterdam-based speech recognition startup Resonate Labs B.V. today released its Rumble-2-Flash transcription model as a free download with open weights.

Designed for fast transcription of prerecorded audio, the 500 million-parameter model supports more than 40 languages. Reson8 is pitching the release at developers and researchers who need speech recognition built for languages other than English.

According to the company, the leading speech models are trained primarily on English, even though only about one in 20 people speak it as a first language. Specialist terms such as medication names are where accuracy is said to fall furthest once speech moves outside English. Reson8’s models are said to be in production use for meeting notetakers, artificial intelligence receptionists, customer support voice agents, medical transcription and captioning.

“Generic speech models are built for English and make noticeably more mistakes in other languages,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Raoul Ritter, who started the company with Thomas Kluiters and Jarno Verhagen. “Languages like Dutch, Swedish and German are spoken by millions, yet they’re an afterthought.”

Reson8 describes Rumble-2-Flash as one of the smallest models on Hugging Face Inc.’s Open ASR Leaderboard. In the company’s own runs of the leaderboard’s multilingual tests, the model averaged a word error rate of 7.09% across seven languages, including German, French and Dutch. Its average error rate in English is claimed to be about 5%.

On a separate test covering 10 lower-resource languages such as Maltese and Basque, Rumble-2-Flash is said to have posted a mean word error rate of 17.6%. OpenAI Group PBC’s Whisper Large V3 had a mean word error rate of 39.82% on the same test, according to Reson8.

Beyond benchmark sets, Reson8’s models are said to be trained for noisy settings, including phone-line audio. The real world “doesn’t happen in a recording studio,” said Kluiters, the company’s head of AI.

Today’s open-weights release follows the model’s Nov. 3 debut in Reson8’s application programming interface, a week before the company launched its flagship Rumble-2 model. Custom vocabulary support, which lets customers add up to 50,000 terms as text without fine-tuning, remains exclusive to Rumble-2.

Hosted on the company’s own graphics processing units in the Netherlands, Reson8’s service is said to retain no audio or transcripts. The company also claims ISO 27001 certification and compliance with the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation and the bloc’s AI Act.

Available free under an Apache 2.0 license, Rumble-2-Flash can also be accessed through Reson8’s API at prices starting from €0.01 ($0.001) per hour of audio.

Reson8 raised €5 million ($5.5 million) in pre-seed funding in March. Balderton Capital led the round, with NP-Hard Ventures also participating. Speech is “quickly becoming a default interface across software,” according to James Wise, a partner at Balderton.

Hilton and Ocasio-Cortez spoke at a news conference outside the Capitol with Rep. Laurel Lee, a Florida Republican and fellow cosponsor. Hilton directed a plea at Speaker Mike Johnson, Majority Leader Steve Scalise and House Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan. "You have the power to move this legislation forward," she said. Hilton said that among the 119th Congress's 156 women, 83 are the subject of sexual deepfakes found online.

#5388. Nvidia is stopping AI chip shipments to China after Jensen Huang's exit

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia sold $2.4 billion of licensed Hopper chips to China last quarter and has none in guidance

Samuel Boivin / NurPhoto via Getty Images

Nvidia $NVDA has stopped shipping licensed Hopper data center chips to China, interim CEO Colette Kress said on an earnings call on Tuesday. The halt comes days after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO.

Nvidia booked $2.4 billion in China sales of licensed Hopper-based data center hardware during the fiscal third quarter, which ended Oct. 25. Kress said the company's forward guidance includes no such products. "Our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China," she said.

Kress gave no reason for the end of the shipments and did not indicate whether the pause would last, according to Reuters. The Hopper family counts the H200 among its chips, a processor that powers both the development and the operation of cutting-edge AI systems.

Huang had pushed harder than anyone at the company for selling chips into the Chinese market, according to Bloomberg. After meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping at a summit last year, President Donald Trump declared that vetted buyers in China could purchase the H200. The arrangement routed eligible chips through the U.S. on their way to China, with a 25% tariff imposed on them when imported into the U.S. Washington cleared 10 Chinese firms to buy the H200, among them Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance, according to Reuters. Beijing has restricted H200 imports.

On Sunday, the Trump administration issued rules that limit sales of advanced U.S. chips to data centers that plan to give Chinese companies remote access. Kress said Nvidia's pile of unfilled orders for high-end products such as Vera Rubin means the rules would not touch its top-line revenue.

Nvidia announced that its board has created a committee whose remit covers export restrictions and national security. Board Chair Harvey Jones said on the call that the board recognizes it is "living in a world" where "national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace." The next CEO will need to "navigate those waters very carefully," Jones said.

Huang, who said Tuesday he would be honored to return as CEO if the board decides it serves shareholders, employees, the company and America, resigned on Nov. 12 after admitting to an affair. The woman is a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer. U.S. intelligence officials suspect she is an agent of Beijing's spy agencies. Beijing has rejected any suggestion that it targeted Huang for espionage.

Jones said the board has hired Heidrick & Struggles to run the search for a permanent CEO and does not intend to reinstate Huang. Kress is serving as interim CEO while keeping her role as chief financial officer.

#5387. Quantum computing drops its decade-away tag as error rates fall 200-fold in two years

Quantum computing is shedding its reputation as speculative as gains in quantum error correction turn fragile machines into reliable ones. For the supercomputing community, which now measures data centers in gigawatts of power, the more pressing question is how quantum fits beside the processors already on the floor.

For years, the field faced a trade-off between speed and reliability, because correcting errors inside a quantum computer slowed it down. That trade-off is fading fast, according to Rajeeb Hazra (pictured), chief executive officer of Quantinuum Inc., which listed on the Nasdaq in June.

“We are now at a stage in 2026 where we have the ability to have tremendous amounts of computation at a very high reliability rate,” Hazra said. “Just two weeks ago, we announced we were doing up to a million operations with five errors. To put it in contrast, just two years ago, we were trying to do 1,000 operations with one error. That’s how fast it is.”

Hazra spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed advances in quantum error correction and how AI and quantum computing work in tandem. (* Disclosure below.)

Quantinuum’s 100-qubit Helios system recently set an error-correction record, reaching logical fidelity equivalent to five errors per million operations. The company builds the full stack, from hardware to developer tools, so customers can model problems such as how a drug ages and loses potency, Hazra explained. That positions quantum less as a rival to AI than as a tool AI will lean on for accurate simulation.

“We see AI and quantum working in tandem, or rather AI using quantum computers,” Hazra said. “I don’t think it’s people using quantum computers; it’s AI programming quantum computers to get the data they need to do what AI does best, which is reasoning and prediction.”

Two cloud service providers have already struck deals with Quantinuum, and most of its use-case customers are commercial companies in pharma, energy, chemicals and financial services, Hazra explained. With quantum error correction maturing, the payoff lies in designing materials that release medicine only where the body needs it.

“My view is in five to seven years max, you’re not going to get a prescription for amoxicillin,” Hazra said. “You’re going to get a sheet of paper that basically says this is your pathology. It’ll get matched up at CVS Pharmacy with the available proteins, if you will, and you will get your personalized medicine.”

By 6:56 a.m. ET on Tuesday, spot gold had dropped 2.3% to $3,762.11 an ounce, having slid as much as 2.4% earlier in the session. Musalem spoke at the Central Bank of Argentina's Money and Banking Conference in Buenos Aires. He said a series of rate hikes will probably be necessary before spring 2027 if price stability is to be reached on a reasonable timeline. He estimated the real policy rate at the lower end of a 1% to 1.5% range and said it should reach a level solidly between 2% and 2.5%.

Minutes from the Fed's October meeting are due for release Wednesday, according to Bloomberg. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gave no direct comment on monetary policy in remarks this week.

The Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% on Oct. 28 after a quarter-point increase in September, with two of 12 voting officials dissenting in favor of a hike. Spot gold traded at $3,956.09 an ounce on Oct. 30 after dipping to its weakest price since June 30.

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said on Nov. 10 that the Fed needs at least two more quarter-point increases and may be able to move faster this winter. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9.

#5384. Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Daily pool data shows Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

According to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

ZecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

Across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:

Together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

October was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

At September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

The deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

NU7 does not introduce a new transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable."

The coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

As of ZecStats' latest update on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

In October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

Small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who plan to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

In practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. Users need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

The September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

That has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

Every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

The useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

#5383. /C O R R E C T I O N - Evoke Security/

In the news release, Evoke Security Launches Defender CTF, the First Hands-On Lab for Investigating AI Agent Incidents, issued Nov. 17, 2026 by Evoke Security over PR Newswire, we are advised by a representative of the company that changes have been made throughout the press release. The complete, corrected release follows:

Built from rogue-agent behavior Evoke sees in live environments, the lab shows security practitioners what agent evidence exists and how to investigate agent-involved security incidents effectively.

WASHINGTON, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Evoke Security, the agent detection and response platform for the agentic workforce, today launched the Evoke Rogue Agent Capture the Flag (CTF), a hands-on lab that trains security practitioners to investigate incidents involving AI agents. Participants work through five staged incidents modeled on agent behavior Evoke has observed in the field. Analysts can see exactly what an investigation into an agent-involved incident requires and what they would miss without the right visibility.

"The next incident most security teams investigate will involve an AI agent," said Jason Rebholz, co-founder of Evoke Security. "Agents are already running commands, moving sensitive data, and taking action across endpoint, SaaS, and cloud systems on behalf of employees. Most security teams have never investigated one, and most don't know which systems hold the evidence they'd need. We want them to learn that now, in a lab, not in the middle of a breach."

Inside the lab, participants get the complete record of what an agent did, drawn from the same data Evoke collects in customer environments: the prompts and instructions the agent received, every tool and MCP server call and what was passed to it, commands executed in the runtime environment, files and records accessed, and actions taken in SaaS applications and cloud services, each tied back to the person and the agent responsible. Participants see where each piece of evidence originates, what it reveals, and how the pieces connect into a single timeline.

The CTF centers on the two most common issues Evoke observes in customer environments: employee misuse of agents and agents that go rogue. Every individual step can look legitimate in isolation. The CTF shows how those steps add up to a security incident, and what it takes to prove it.

Working the case, participants separate what the user asked for from what the agent actually did, pinpoint where the agent went beyond its instructions, flag the suspicious behavior, and reconstruct the incident timeline. They also see how much of the case disappears without agent telemetry. Many teams can already pull in agent activity, from AI providers' compliance and audit logs to endpoint, SIEM, and identity data. What they cannot do today with existing tools is tie those sources into a single view that shows what the agent did and where it crossed the line, leaving threats missed and investigations stalled.

"Every investigation comes down to evidence. Security teams tell me every week how painful it is to collect agent telemetry, let alone conduct an investigation," said Jason Rebholz, co-founder of Evoke Security. "We built the Rogue Agent CTF so practitioners can see how the right detections, with the right evidence readily available, make investigations fast and easy."

The Rogue Agent CTF is practitioner-specific training for incident responders, SOC analysts, threat hunters, and detection engineers, and is designed by Evoke's team of incident responders, who bring breach investigation experience from Mandiant. Participants leave with a working map of where agent evidence comes from and how to use it in an investigation, plus a clear view of the visibility gaps in their own environment.

Test your investigative skills and see what it takes to investigate an AI agent incident. Access the Evoke Rogue Agent CTF.

Evoke Security is the agent detection and response platform built to secure the agentic workforce. Founded by incident response veterans, Evoke enables security teams to continuously inventory, threat model, and monitor AI agents, stopping risky agent behavior in real time. Evoke treats agents as the next operating system for business, surfacing risky configurations and analyzing agent actions so organizations can adopt agents without compounding security debt.
